title: Your absurd name,
html_source:
This whole consideration of Stephen’s name may allude to the first chapter of A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man, where “Nasty Roche” asks Stephen, “What kind of name is that?” Stephen was unable to answer, and here, Mulligan considers its derivation and “The mockery of it”.

Buck Mulligan may be specifically referring to Stephen’s first name, being the name of the first Christian Martyr, but more likely he is concerned by the incongruous nature of an Irishman having the name of a mythological Ancient Greek—by the same token, this might be wry self-comment on Joyce’s outlandish choice of name for his protagonist and alter-ego.

Stephen’s name also ties in with the conflict and commingling of Hebraism and Hellenism (very roughly, Jewishness and Ancient Greekness) throughout the novel.
